questions.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{2}$ at the point $(2,8)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $p+q.$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})=4x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2)=4(2)=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-8 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-2) \\ 8y-64 & =-x+2 \\ x+8y & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p+q=8+66=74.$

questions.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{5}-2x$ at the point $(1,0)$ is given by $y=ax+b$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants. Find the value of $a+b.$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{5}-2x.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{5}-2x)=10{x}^{4}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=10(1)^{4}-2=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-0 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-1) \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a+b=-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{8}=0.$

questions.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}$ at the point $(1,4)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $q-p.$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\right) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =-2{x}^{-3/2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{{1}^{3}}}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-1) \\ 2y-8 & =x-1 \\ x-2y & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $q-p=-7-(-2)=-5.$

Therefore, $p-q=-9-(-26)=17.$

canonical_example.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=x^3 - x^2$ at the point $(1,0)$ is given by $y=px+q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the values of $p$ and $q.$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^3 - x^2.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-{x}^{2})=3{x}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1, 0){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=3-2=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line $m'$ is

$$
m'=-\dfrac{1}{m}=-1.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-0 & =-(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-1$ and $q=1.$
